title: Chemical Bonding I (Ionic & Covalent) - Chemistry - Covalent Bonding
subject: Chemistry

options: One atom completely takes an electron from another.
The attraction between two nuclei and a shared pair of electrons exceeds the repulsion between the nuclei and electrons.
Two metal atoms share a sea of electrons.
Van der Waals forces hold two atoms close together.
questions.explain: Covalent bonds represent a balance where the attraction of each nucleus for the shared electrons overcomes the repulsion between the two positively charged nuclei.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which general relationship exists between bond length and bond strength for covalent bonds between the same two atoms?
options: As bond length increases, bond strength increases.
As bond length decreases, bond strength increases.
Bond length and bond strength are unrelated.
Bond strength is determined solely by the atomic mass.
questions.explain: Shorter bonds are generally stronger. For example, a triple bond is shorter and stronger than a double bond, which is shorter and stronger than a single bond.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Using electronegativity values ($\\chi$), which of the following bonds corresponds to a 'polar covalent' bond?
options: A bond where $\Delta\chi$ is between 0.4 and 1.8 (e.g., H-Cl)
A bond where electrons are shared equally.
questions.explain: Bonds with an electronegativity difference between roughly 0.4 and 1.8 are considered polar covalent, where electrons are shared unequally but not transferred completely.
